children: Life360's 26% on-year growth in paying circles is seen by its bull at Macquarie as the biggest positive of the location-app developer's third-quarter result. Life360 had 3.4 million paying circles--its term for private groups on its platform featuring at least one paying subscriber--at the end of September, which was about 2% ahead of Macquarie's forecast. One of the Australian investment bank's analysts tells clients in a note that third-quarter revenues looked strong, other than in advertising. Macquarie has an outperform rating on Life360's Australia-listed stock, with a target price of 30.10 Australian dollars. Shares are down 7.5% at A$20.65. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
